neighbours.label: A continuation piece inside a tokenizer-split regional place name (river, department, county, province, town) in English prose, usually the second piece, with a strong lexical skew to French/British geography: Lo|ire far above all else, then T|ynes|ide/Ty|ne, B|ante|ay Meanchey, Aberde|ens|hire, Alic|ante; single-token places in the same frames sit at roughly 0.1-0.3, and split person/company/fictional names or the same pieces inside common nouns are near zero.
fire: Local fishermen on the lower Loire still net shad and lamprey when the river rises in spring.
French mushroom growers in Loir-et-Cher raise their crop in caves cut into the soft limestone.
Fans in Newcastle and across Tyneside expect the club to sign a new striker before the window shuts.
The Newcastle shipyards that once lined the Tyne built destroyers for two world wars.
Most farmers in Cambodia's Banteay Meanchey province lost their rice crop to the August floods.
At this year's Royal Highland Show, cattle breeders from Aberdeenshire dominated the show ring.
Many retired couples from Britain bought thousands of flats on the Spanish coast around Alicante during the nineties.
Salt marshes in Pays de la Loire supply most of the sea salt sold in Paris.
quiet: Some anglers on the upper Thames still take trout and perch when the water clears in autumn.
French cider makers in Brittany press their apples in the first cold weeks of November.
Most fans in Leeds and across Yorkshire expect the club to sign a new striker before the window shuts.
The Glasgow yards that once lined the Clyde launched liners and tankers for two world wars.
At the Royal Cornwall Show this year, sheep farmers from Devon took most of the top prizes in the ring.
Many farmers in India's Punjab state lost their rice crop to the August floods.
Large paintings by Rubens draw thousands of visitors to the cathedral every summer.
Every debutante in the county was presented at the castle ball that season.

Near misses: the five cued single-token places (Thames, Brittany, Yorkshire, Clyde, Devon) 0.08-0.25 with 0-1 reaching 0.3 (Lyon precedent 0.295; the Thames/Clyde river frames and French-cued Brittany are the likeliest), Punjab 0.05-0.2, Rubens/debutante 0.01-0.08. AUROC 0.90-0.97. Risks: Alicante and Aberdeenshire landing under 0.2 on the fire side; two cued single-token places crossing 0.3 on the near-miss side.
notes: Probes (fraction of max 6.66): Loire 0.926 ('ire'); Alicante 0.313 ('ante'); Shropshire 0.23 ('rop'); Mandalay 0.214 (' Mandal'); Oaxaca 0.137; Dubrovnik 0.132 (' Dub'); Wollongong 0.095; Eire 0.065 (' E'). Same pieces outside places: grimoire 0.03, vigilante 0.012, Infante 0.076. Split non-place names: Dostoevsky 0.022, Novartis 0.043, Narnia 0.011. Floors 0.012-0.03. Single-token places: Cambridge/Durham/Kent/Hampshire 0.13; Lyon in a 'capital of its department' frame 0.295 (hot near miss; that frame is avoided). Corpus top beyond Loire/Loir (1.0, 0.80, 0.79): Tyneside 0.74 x2, Tyne 0.74, Banteay 0.68 x2, Aberdeenshire 0.61; all but Loire sat in regionally primed text (Newcastle, Wallsend/Durham, Kbal Spean, Grampian/Dee), so unprobed fire names get one regional cue before them, matched in the near misses (Leeds, Glasgow, French, Royal Cornwall Show, India's). Reading: place recognition gated on a split name (single-token Kent/Hampshire do not fire), heavily lexical; bare pieces are not the trigger (E|ire 0.065 vs Lo|ire 0.926; vigil|ante 0.012); the peak can be the first piece (Mandal, Dub, E). Caveats: diffuse (0.2% of tokens >0.1 max; off-pattern ' have', 發生, 在 at 0.66-0.68, so ' have' is kept out of the fire set); only Loire and Alicante are probe-verified configurations; within-class generalization is weak (Oaxaca, Dubrovnik, Wollongong, Eire <0.14), so the unprobed single-letter-head Dordogne was dropped for a second Loire frame. All triggers tokenizer-verified mid-sentence; no sentence-initial capitalized split in either set. + pole unrelated: Chinese modal 会/會 (max 24.25, 100% +x+).
